question: If 3x + 7 = 25, what is the value of x?
explanation: Subtract 7: 3x = 18. Divide by 3: x = 6.

question: If x + y = 14 and x − y = 4, what is the value of xy?
explanation: Add the equations: 2x = 18, so x = 9 and y = 5. xy = 45.

question: A line in the xy-plane passes through (2, 5) and (6, 17). What is the y-coordinate of its y-intercept?
The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 4x + 1. What is f(3)?
What is the positive solution to x² − 5x − 14 = 0?
explanation: Factor: (x − 7)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 7 or x = −2. The positive one is 7.

question: If (2^x)(2^(x + 3)) = 2^11, what is the value of x?
explanation: Add exponents: 2x + 3 = 11, so x = 4.

question: A jacket costs $40. It is on sale for 15% off. What is the sale price?
The mean of 5 numbers is 12. When a sixth number is added, the mean becomes 13. What is the sixth number?
explanation: Sum of 5 numbers = 60. Sum of 6 numbers = 78. 78 − 60 = 18.

question: A right triangle has legs of length 9 and 12. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
A circle in the xy-plane has equation x² + y² − 6x + 8y = 0. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation: Complete the square: (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 25. The radius is √25 = 5.

passage: After weeks of rain, the farmers were relieved when the forecast finally called for a ______ stretch of dry, sunny days, giving them time to harvest their crops.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
explanation: The farmers need a long, continuous dry period to harvest. "Sustained" means lasting.

passage: Many people assume that city parks exist only for recreation. Urban planner Dana Okafor argues that parks also do practical work: their trees cool nearby streets, and their soil absorbs rainwater that would otherwise flood storm drains. In one study of a midsize city, neighborhoods next to large parks had fewer flooded basements after heavy storms.
question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It explains a problem and then lists several unrelated solutions.
choices.B: It tells the history of city parks from earliest to most recent.
choices.C: It compares two cities and concludes one is better designed.
choices.D: It describes a common view, presents a broader view, and gives evidence for the broader view.

explanation: The text starts with an assumption (parks are for recreation), adds Okafor's view (they also do practical work), then cites a study.

passage: Biologists studying a species of desert lizard noticed that lizards living near rocky hillsides had longer back legs than lizards living on flat sand. Longer legs help a lizard jump between rocks. When the researchers moved some flat-sand lizards to a rocky area, the lizards' offspring, raised among the rocks, had longer legs than their parents. This suggests that ______
question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: rocky hillsides contain more food than flat sand.
choices.B: leg length in these lizards is influenced by the environment in which they grow up.
choices.C: lizards on flat sand cannot survive among rocks.
choices.D: longer legs make lizards slower on sand.

explanation: Offspring of flat-sand lizards grew longer legs when raised among rocks, so the environment affects leg length. The other choices are not supported.

passage: A student surveyed four school clubs about how many hours per week members spend on club activities. Chess Club: 3 hours. Robotics Club: 7 hours. Drama Club: 5 hours. Debate Club: 4 hours. The student claims that Robotics Club members spend more time on club activities than members of any other club surveyed.
question: Which choice best uses the data to support the student's claim?

choices.A: Debate Club members spend 1 hour more than Chess Club members.
choices.B: Chess Club members spend 3 hours per week, the fewest of any club.
choices.C: Drama Club and Debate Club members together spend 9 hours per week.
choices.D: Robotics Club members spend 7 hours per week, more than the 5 hours spent by Drama Club, the next highest.

explanation: Only D compares Robotics to the next-highest club, which shows it is the highest.

passage: Marisol started a small community garden on an empty lot in her neighborhood. At first, only a few neighbors helped. Within two years, more than forty families were growing vegetables there, and the garden was hosting weekend cooking classes. Neighbors who had never spoken before now shared tools and recipes.
question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.B: Cooking classes are popular on weekends.
choices.C: A community garden grew over time and brought neighbors together.
choices.D: Vegetables grow best on empty city lots.

explanation: The text focuses on the garden growing and connecting neighbors. The other choices are minor details or unsupported.

passage: The museum's new exhibit features over two hundred handmade quilts ______ some of them are more than a century old.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Both parts are complete sentences, so a semicolon joins them. A comma alone or no punctuation creates a run-on.

passage: The collection of old maps stored in the library's basement ______ visitors from all over the state.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is "collection," which is singular, so it needs the singular verb "attracts."

passage: Engineer Tomas ______ designed a bridge that bends slightly in strong wind instead of cracking.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Reyes, who grew up near the coast,
choices.B: Reyes who grew up near the coast,
choices.C: Reyes, who grew up near the coast
choices.D: Reyes; who grew up near the coast,

explanation: The clause "who grew up near the coast" is extra information, so it needs a comma on both sides.

passage: Electric buses produce no exhaust while driving, which improves air quality on busy streets. ______ they cost more to buy than diesel buses, so many cities have been slow to switch.
question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence gives a drawback that contrasts with the benefit, so "However" fits.

passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Honeybees communicate the location of food using a "waggle dance."
• The direction of the dance shows the direction of the food relative to the sun.
• The length of the waggle shows how far away the food is.
• Researcher Lena Brandt recorded over 500 dances in one summer.
question: The student wants to explain how the waggle dance communicates distance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Honeybees communicate in many ways, including dancing.
choices.B: In a honeybee's waggle dance, the length of the waggle tells other bees how far away the food is.
choices.C: Lena Brandt recorded over 500 honeybee dances in one summer.
choices.D: Honeybees use a waggle dance, and its direction relates to the sun.

explanation: Only B explains how the dance shows distance, which is the student's goal.
